claims.text: The syllabus’s NIC examples include South Africa and India. South Africa’s public transport and electricity networks illustrate shared infrastructure used in industrial production; India’s public technical education and research illustrate support for productive skills and knowledge. Neither example proves that a single policy caused growth or that services are currently reliable. More generally a state can coordinate investment, improve export links or support access to finance. These measures have opportunity costs and can fail through poor selection or weak accountability. Test actual use, access and productive benefit rather than the spending total.

claims.text: Namibian examples include mineral extraction and processing, fish processing, meat processing and tourism-related services. A fish-processing activity can add local handling, packaging and transport work to landed fish, provided stocks and quality are protected. Meat processing can connect livestock producers with slaughtering, storage and marketing. Mineral processing can retain a production stage locally but needs power, skills and buyers; mining income alone does not establish benefits for every household. Tourism creates service demand where local guides, accommodation and suppliers participate. These examples identify established activities, not current employment totals or a ranking of their size.
